title: a layer wrapped in a type-only satisfies that genuinely does not provide a capability the body requires is refused for that capability by name, not as an unreadable layer
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Satisfaction': 'When the compiler knows the complete closure, an unsatisfied capability MUST be a compile error.' The wrapper here is `satisfies Layer<typeof Clock>`, which is type-only and true: the operand really is a `Layer<typeof Clock>`. So the closure IS known, and the answer must be the precise one — `SMITHERS2101` naming Directory, the capability `stamped` requires and the layer does not supply. WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE CASE FROM THE ACCEPTING ONE: `a-layer-through-a-type-only-wrapper-is-the-same-layer` shows eight wrappers keeping their acceptance, and a wrapper-stripping fix can pass that case while degrading every REFUSAL under a wrapper into the opaque verdict. This case is the discriminator, and the discrimination is the whole content: `SMITHERS2104` ('this layer expression cannot be read') and `SMITHERS2101` ('this layer really is missing Directory') are two different statements about a program, and only the second one tells the author what to fix. Before the 2026-08-27 fork fix the corpus could not express the difference at all — `SMITHERS2104` had exactly one case and no case anywhere put a wrapper near a layer — which is why 143 divergent cells closed with conformance reporting 0 divergent throughout. `messageContains` is declared, and the payload IS the promise here: code and position alone are satisfied by a refusal naming Clock, the capability that WAS supplied, which is precisely the shape of a backend that computed the provided set and the required set the wrong way round. It is the capability's bare name rather than the rendered row because the two backends render a row differently — the reference prints `Directory` where the fork prints `{Directory}` — so the bare name is the smallest fragment carrying the obligation on both. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: the wrapper's own type. `satisfies Layer<typeof Clock>` is written truthfully on purpose, so that this case says nothing about whether an ASSERTED type is believed — that is `a-laundering-assertion-does-not-change-which-capability-a-layer-provides`, its direct sibling, where the assertion lies. Keeping the two apart means a future 'resolve the layer from its checker type' rewrite turns the sibling red without this one changing meaning. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the declared column from 23 to 24 turns the case red on BOTH backends with the position diff printed, and separately mutating the declared `messageContains` from `Directory` to `Clock` turns it red on both with the message diff printed; the file was restored byte-identically after each (sha256 dcefd11609ee40ca6e96c6dd13a274d46124ddc4b740210e018dbfbf88d51b06 before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently). The paired positive control is `a-layer-through-a-type-only-wrapper-is-the-same-layer`, which must keep compiling AND RUNNING, so a fix that answers `SMITHERS2101` for every wrapped layer turns that case red instead of passing quietly.
